Trace, implement and test: Next Prime

Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
#include <iostream>
#include <cmath>
using namespace std;

// Function to check if a number is prime
bool isPrime(int n) {
    if (n <= 1)
        return false;
    for (int i = 2; i <= sqrt(n); i++) {
        if (n % i == 0)
            return false;
    }
    return true;
}

// Function to find the next prime number after n
int nextPrime(int n) {
    int candidate = n + 1;
    while (true) {
        if (isPrime(candidate))
            return candidate;
        candidate++;
    }
}

// Function to check if the second number is the next prime after the first
bool isNextPrime(int prime1, int prime2) {
    if (!isPrime(prime1) || !isPrime(prime2))
        return false;
    return nextPrime(prime1) == prime2;
}

int main() {
    int num1, num2;
    cout << "Enter two numbers: ";
    cin >> num1 >> num2;

    if (isNextPrime(num1, num2)) {
        cout << "True" << endl;
    } else {
        cout << "False" << endl;
    }

    return 0;
}
